The early access label is an excuse for a janky game that is constantly getting updates no one asked for. They change what little good the game has, but never change any of the bad, like the giant maps that’re empty. Once playable maps, are now a damn lag simulator, and I don’t even play on that low end of a PC. This game has made about $260 million dollars, yet the studio seems to genuinely mainly care about overpriced merch. The updates are so few and far between, and when they do come, they’re lackluster or worse, do more harm than good by adding bad content and bugs. The dev team for some reason seem to have a bad relationship with the community, and I cannot for the life of me think of any reason why. The reason you guys are STANDING as a team and company is because of fans, but you shut us down and dismiss us, and discourage anything that goes outside of the narrative you guys so desperately want. They’re strongly against mods for the weirdest reason, I mean what the hell man, you would get even more plays and diversity in the game if you allowed or encouraged it. This game was fun and interesting at one point. It was janky, but more so in a lovable way, where you could tell it was a little rough, but made with love. But recently, with all the unnecessary changes, the way the dev team acts towards us, and the way the game is handled as a whole, the past 2 or so years leaves such a bad taste in my mouth, and the game feels more like a chore now than anything. 4/10 for me

Phasmophobia is exactly the kind of ghost-hunting chaos I want. The problem is that I have no friends to play it with. Which is rude, because this game is clearly built for group panic. I want to walk into a haunted house with a flashlight, a dream, and the confidence of someone who has watched way too much Sam and Colby. I want to ask ghosts disrespectful questions, immediately regret it, and then scream because something moved in the kitchen. The whole setup is so good. You gather evidence, use equipment, watch for signs, try to figure out what kind of ghost you are dealing with, and then attempt to leave before it turns your investigation into a funeral announcement. It is creepy, funny, stressful, and so much better when everyone is panicking together. One person is trying to be serious. One person is already hiding in the van. One person is yelling the ghost’s name like they have never heard of consequences. That is the dream. Even without a full group, I still love the idea of it. The atmosphere is tense, the ghost mechanics are fun, and every investigation feels like it could go from “we are professionals” to “absolutely not, goodbye” in half a second. Phasmophobia lets me live my Sam and Colby dreams, or at least it would if my friends would get their lives together and play with me. Until then, I am just standing outside the haunted house with equipment, trust issues, and no backup.
